findings.title: Google refresh persists the Zod result and corrupts credentials
findings.body: After every Google token refresh, the code assigns `key` to the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` and writes that object to `credential.key`. That helper returns the Zod safeParse result (`{ success, data }`), not the credential payload. Previously this path stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`. The next calendar use calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and fails, so a normal token refresh (syncing disabled) permanently breaks that user's Google Calendar connection until the app is reconnected.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
findings.body: If the parsed token body has no `refresh_token`, this helper sets `data.refresh_token` to the string `"refresh_token"` and returns that object. Office 365's refresh schema treats `refresh_token` as optional because Microsoft often omits it and expects the client to keep the existing one; `Office365CalendarService` then spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential and saves it. The real refresh token is overwritten with the placeholder, so the next refresh fails and the Outlook connection is dead. The same placeholder is copied onto Zoom tokens whenever the sync parser is used.

findings.title: Sync token schema cannot accept a real token response
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, refresh bodies are validated with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` are the literal property names of those Zod types (e.g. "ZodString"), not a catchall, and Zod objects strip unknown keys by default. A normal `{ access_token, expires_in }` body therefore fails validation and every synced refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Even a passing parse would drop `expires_in`, so callers such as Zoom that do `Date.now() + expires_in * 1000` would store `NaN` and immediately treat the token as expired.

findings.title: Sync refresh returns a raw fetch Response that callers cannot use
findings.body: When syncing is on, this helper returns the `fetch` Response and does not check `response.ok`, set `Content-Type`, or parse JSON. Callers were not updated to that shape: Google reads `res.data` (undefined on a Response, so the refresh throws and can mark the credential invalid), HubSpot treats the Response as a token and computes `expiryDate` from `expiresIn` (NaN) before `setAccessToken(undefined)`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data` as if it were an axios response. Lark still runs `handleLarkError` expecting a Lark envelope, but the comment says the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry. Token refresh for those apps fails as soon as `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, which is the documented test path.

findings.title: Salesforce client refresh calls prisma without importing it and keeps the old access token
findings.body: `getClient` now always POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then calls `prisma.credential.update`, but `prisma` is not imported in this file, so constructing a Salesforce calendar service throws ReferenceError before any event work. The new access token is also never passed into `jsforce.Connection` (`accessToken` stays `credentialKey.access_token`). This runs for every Salesforce credential, including when sync is disabled, and hardcoding `login.salesforce.com` fails sandbox and My Domain orgs that previously relied on the stored `instance_url`. It also never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync does not apply to Salesforce.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sync sends credential id as calcomUserId
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` with `credentialId` as the third argument. That argument is sent as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. The parent app will look up the wrong user (or none) and return another user's tokens or an error, so Bigin refresh cannot succeed in sync mode. Other adapters correctly pass `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Zoom sync uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
findings.body: The refresh call passes `"zoomvideo"` as `appSlug`, but Zoom credentials are stored and addressed everywhere else as app id `"zoom"` (see the OAuth callback and the webhook's `appSlug` lookup). A self-hoster syncing by app slug will not find the Zoom credential and will refresh the wrong app or fail.

findings.title: Credential webhook can duplicate or leave stale invalid credentials
findings.body: The handler does `findFirst` by `userId` + `appId` and then create-or-update with no transaction and no `invalid: false`. Concurrent deliveries can both miss the row and insert two credentials; later reads use `findFirst` and ignore the other. An update of a credential already marked `invalid` keeps `invalid: true`, so synced tokens are never used. `schema.parse` and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` are also uncaught, so a bad body or ciphertext becomes an unhandled 500 instead of 4xx, and there is no method check so non-POST requests are processed the same way.
